request.title: The Guilty Look Isn't Guilt
request.provider_topic: Does a dog's guilty look mean the dog feels guilty?
request.narration: That guilty look? It isn't a confession. In a 2009 study, fourteen dogs were left with food. Sometimes owners were told the dog had eaten, even when it hadn't. When owners returned, the guilty look tracked the scolding. Dogs looked guiltier when scolded, whether or not they had taken the food. In other words, the look tracked the owner's cues, not a reliable inner sense of guilt. The dogs were reading the moment. The paper describes the look as lowered head, flattened ears, and a tucked tail — a package humans readily read as guilt. So skip the interrogation. Check what actually happened, and respond to the behavior you can see. The look is real; the guilt story is the guess.
